answer: Agents can require every new trading identity to post a bond in a scarce resource and earn access through long-lived, cross-checked work histories: independent agents randomly audit tasks, and conflicting or fabricated reports trigger slashing of the bond and loss of reputation. A sybil attacker must fund many deposits, wait for each identity to mature, and risk correlated losses when its copies coordinate. The result is an economy where cheap fake names fail to buy trust across tundra, ember markets, or a safe haven.
